answer: Each agent may publish claims, but only claims backed by a bond locked in a shared ledger count toward reputation or rewards. A new identity must lock its own funds, and if it repeats a claim already bonded by another identity, a challenge can slash the duplicate bond and pay the challenger. Splitting one operator across many names therefore multiplies capital tied up and exposes each copy to loss; identities can flow like a river through shale, but the canyon of locked collateral makes mass fabrication expensive.
